title: Unfortunately I was very late to getting to see this one and the show...
transcript: You know a show is wild when the fact that its star is almost completely naked the entire show is not even top five wildest things about it. This is one of those shows that starts and you're just like, this is insane. And it somehow manages to continue, one upping itself as it goes. The very loose premise behind this show is that Garry Starr is attempting to recreate all of the novels published under the Penguins classic banner. Now, if you're thinking Ben, there are literally thousands of novels published under Penguins classics. There is no way he is able to recreate all of them in just an hour- You would be correct. He only gets through probably less than 100 of them. And the term recreation I am using very loosely, as most of the “recreations” are just sight gag puns created off of the book’s title. So, for example, to recreate The Grapes of wrath, he has a grape war with one of the audience members where they throw grapes back and forth at each other. So if you were worried that you wouldn't understand this show because you haven't read that many classic novels, don't worry. I don't think he has either. But I don't say that as a negative. This show is incredibly fun, and you truly never know what title or bit is going to come next. And there is a lot of audience participation in this show. In fact, some of the Most intense audience participation that I have ever seen. It is all voluntary, of course, but every time an audience member was chosen, I was like, what is he going to make them do this time? It is, of course, completely voluntary, and anytime there was a particularly intense one, he was very careful to get ample consent first. But it really does build such a community in the room. Like, you are always rooting for the audience volunteer, sometimes in disbelief that they are actually doing the thing that they were instructed to do. And I really don't wanna say much more for fear of giving anything else away, because the fun really is in the surprise of it all. But I will say, if you like clowning, if you like word play and puns, if you like heavy audience participation, I think you're really gonna like this show. Like I said, it's weird, but in the best way, And I can promise you, like nothing you have ever seen before or will ever see again. Gary Starr classic Penguins is going to be a Broadway Ben recommendation.
